purpose: How a website-and-hosting reseller turns a signed small-business site package into a launched, verified site through one repeatable stack and pipeline - build-order translation, content intake with a deadline rule, design-system assembly, third-party integrations proven from the visitor's side, staged client review, quality/performance/accessibility gates, and a domain/DNS/email cutover that never breaks the client's existing business - communicated in plain language with disclosure before every irreversible step, and ending in a documented handoff into care-plan operations.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the operator is a one-person or tiny-team reseller building small marketing sites (roughly ten pages or fewer) for local small businesses
a signed productized scope from the offer stage exists before delivery begins; delivery executes it and never renegotiates the sale
the client retains ownership of their domain, content, and accounts throughout; the operator works through delegated access
performance and accessibility statements are made as measurable per-site checks, never as universal numbers or certifications
accessibility, privacy-notice, and cookie-disclosure obligations vary by jurisdiction; the operator verifies current rules where each client operates
parts of the delivered site are other companies' services the operator does not control - booking, ordering, review, map, chat and payment vendors the client contracts directly
exclusions: offer design, package pricing, care-plan tier design, niche selection, referral acquisition, and scope negotiation - the productized-offer KB owns those
hosting portfolio architecture, backup/update/security operations after launch, monthly reporting, retention, reactivation, and offboarding - the hosting-and-care-plans KB owns those
SEO, traffic, or ranking guarantees of any kind; this KB covers only verifiable on-page craft and continuity of URLs the business already earned
invented market rates or firm prices for builds, hosting, or care plans; money appears only as mechanisms and decisions made at the offer stage
holding a client's domain, content, files, or credentials as leverage; every asset stays client-owned and the exit path stays open by design
custom web-application or full e-commerce platform development beyond the small-business marketing-site scope

selecting or contracting the client's booking, ordering, payment or review vendors, and operating those vendor accounts on the client's behalf; delivery integrates what the client owns and tests it, nothing more

competency_questions.question: How do I turn a signed package into an executable build order that settles later scope arguments without renegotiating the sale?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCOPE_TO_BUILD_TRANSLATION specifies the build order's contents (page list, features, content responsibility matrix, revision allowance, date anchors) and its role as the delivery-side contract of record

competency_questions.question: What criteria justify the one build stack the whole client book runs on, and what would make me change it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STACK_SELECTION_CRITERIA names the reseller-specific criteria (solo maintainability at portfolio scale, client exit portability, hosting fit, security surface, edit speed) and the exception and re-evaluation triggers

competency_questions.question: How does a reusable design system plus a one-job-per-page architecture keep fixed-price builds profitable without every client's site looking identical?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TEMPLATE_DESIGN_SYSTEM explains section-library assembly with per-client token skinning and SITE_ARCHITECTURE_PAGE_PLAN explains the small-site page plan with a stated job and primary action per page

competency_questions.question: How do I get client content on time, and what exactly happens when it never arrives?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTENT_INTAKE_PIPELINE describes the structured intake pack, deadline, and proceed-with-drafts rule, and COPY_AND_MEDIA_STANDARDS sets the copy honesty and media preparation bar the content must clear

competency_questions.question: What does the standardized staging build pass include, and why is the contact form treated as the highest-stakes feature on the site?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BUILD_EXECUTION_CHECKLIST gives the fixed build order on staging and FORMS_AND_LEAD_ROUTING requires authenticated notification, stored submissions, and an end-to-end test to the client's real inbox

competency_questions.question: How are client review rounds run so feedback converges to sign-off instead of looping forever?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STAGING_REVIEW_WORKFLOW describes complete-site reveals, consolidated per-round feedback lists, the revision allowance, out-of-scope routing, and written sign-off as the launch trigger

competency_questions.question: What quality, performance, and accessibility baseline must every site clear before launch, and how are the claims kept verifiable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUALITY_BASELINE_GATE lists the binary pre-launch checks, PERFORMANCE_BASELINE ties every speed claim to a recorded reproducible measurement, and ACCESSIBILITY_BASELINE states the WCAG-informed floor honestly as a baseline rather than a certification

competency_questions.question: How is the client's domain handled so the client always owns it and could leave tomorrow?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DOMAIN_OWNERSHIP_CONTROL requires a client-owned registrar account with delegated operator access, confirmed auto-renew, and an absolute rule against parking client domains in the operator's own account

competency_questions.question: How do I plan a DNS cutover that cannot take down the client's email?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EMAIL_CONTINUITY_SAFEGUARD requires a pre-change inventory and verbatim preservation of mail-carrying records, and DNS_CUTOVER_PLAN specifies zone export, minimal change, TTL lowering, a rollback, and post-switch verification including a mail test

competency_questions.question: What HTTPS and security setup is standard at launch, and how is client control preserved while access is hardened?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SSL_AND_SECURITY_SETUP requires a verified auto-renewing certificate, forced HTTPS redirects, per-person credentials with the client holding owner-level access and the operator working least-privilege

competency_questions.question: What does the launch run cover, and how is the web equity an existing business already earned preserved through a rebuild?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LAUNCH_CHECKLIST_EXECUTION scripts the go-live run with live-domain re-tests and a post-launch watch window, and REDIRECT_AND_CONTINUITY_MAP requires a pre-launch crawl and a complete legacy-URL redirect map verified after cutover

competency_questions.question: What must the client possess at handover, and what definition-of-done moves a launched site into care-plan operations?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLIENT_TRAINING_HANDOVER delivers the asset-and-credential handover pack plus owner training, BUILD_DOCUMENTATION_RUNBOOK produces a takeover-ready per-site record, and CARE_PLAN_HANDOFF_GATE states the pass conditions including backup baseline and written warranty terms

competency_questions.question: Which third-party embeds does this site depend on, who owns each vendor account, and how do I prove each one actually works before launch?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THIRD_PARTY_EMBED_INTEGRATION supplies a per-embed record naming the client-owned vendor account, the visitor-side functional test (a real booking or order the owner confirms receiving), the embed's measured cost against the page budget, its browser-storage footprint so the privacy notice can be honest, and the documented behavior when the vendor is slow or down; PERFORMANCE_BASELINE supplies the measurement that adjudicates weight disputes and QUALITY_BASELINE_GATE reads each test result as a binary pre-launch item.

competency_questions.question: How do I keep delivery communication honest with an owner who cannot verify a single technical claim I make, especially before an irreversible cutover?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONEST_DELIVERY_COMMUNICATION requires progress and risk stated in plain language, every claim paired with a test a skeptic could re-run, written informed consent naming the worst case before any irreversible step, a standing ban on using downtime, hacking or ranking fear as leverage to sell during delivery, and slower written handling with a trusted second person where the owner is out of their depth; DNS_CUTOVER_PLAN supplies the risk and rollback content that consent is given against, and CLIENT_TRAINING_HANDOVER shows what genuine possession at the end looks like.

glossary.definition: The delivery-side restatement of the signed package: exact page list, included features, who supplies each content item by when, the revision allowance, and the schedule anchors; later scope questions are settled by pointing at it.

The constrained set of pre-built, brand-skinnable page sections (hero, services grid, testimonial band, gallery, contact block) plus a fixed type scale that new sites are assembled from instead of designed from a blank canvas.

The kickoff agreement that if client content misses its deadline, the operator drafts professional copy from the intake questionnaire and public materials and the build continues, with the client correcting at staging review.
The private, search-engine-excluded environment where the site is built and reviewed; nothing is constructed or edited on the live domain during the build.

A per-site cap on page weight and script load enforced by mechanism (images compressed to display size, limited webfonts, no purposeless plugins, host caching) and proven by a repeatable recorded lab measurement.
A complete saved copy of every DNS record on the client's domain - including MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and subdomains - taken before any change so nothing is lost or reconstructed from memory.
Reducing DNS record time-to-live values a day or more before a cutover so that both the switch and any rollback propagate quickly instead of lingering for hours.

The rebuild artifact pairing every crawled legacy URL with its successor page (or a deliberate retirement target) so no inbound link, listing, or printed QR code the business already earned hits a 404.

Working inside the client's registrar, hosting, or analytics account through an invited collaborator role the client can revoke, instead of the operator holding the client's own login or owning the account.
The written post-launch period during which defects in the delivered build are fixed at no charge, separating build accountability from the ongoing paid care plan that follows.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for site_build_stack_and_delivery_process work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Convert the signed productized package into an executable build order before any work starts: the exact page list, the features included (contact form, map, gallery, booking link), which template family and library sections will be used, who supplies each content item and by when, the included revision allowance restated, and the date anchors for content deadline, staging review, and launch window. The build order is the delivery-side contract of record - every later dispute about what is in or out is settled by pointing at it, never by renegotiating the sale, which belongs to the offer stage and stays there.

included: content responsibility matrix with due dates
excluded: any change to what was sold

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a scope dispute or change-order pattern reveals a category the build-order template fails to capture

pros.claim: A written build order turns vague expectations into checkable line items
pros.example: when a bakery owner asks for a fifth service page mid-build, the order shows the package included four, so the request routes to a change order instead of an argument

cons.claim: A rigid order can force pedantic change orders for trivial asks that goodwill would absorb
cons.example: invoicing paperwork to swap two photos the client sent late sours an otherwise happy referral source

failure_modes: starting the build from the proposal email thread instead of an itemized order
leaving content responsibility unstated so every missing item silently becomes the operator's job
acceptance_tests: the build order lists every page and feature, names the content owner and due date per item, restates the revision allowance, and carries the client's written acknowledgment
revisit_triggers: the client requests something not on the order
the offer stage changes the package definition upstream

nodes.definition: Choose one build stack the whole book of clients runs on, and re-justify it deliberately rather than per project. The criteria that matter for a reseller: a solo operator can maintain dozens of sites on it; the client can leave with a working site because a real export path exists; it fits low-cost portfolio hosting; its plugin and extension surface is small enough to secure and update; common edits take minutes not hours; and other practitioners exist who could substitute for the operator. Whether that lands on a mainstream CMS with one page-builder standard, a static generator with a lightweight CMS, or a managed builder matters less than that there is exactly one default and every deviation is a written exception with an owner.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the platform's ownership, pricing, export path, or ecosystem health materially changes

pros.claim: One stack means every fix learned once applies across the whole portfolio
pros.example: a plugin vulnerability patched with one tested procedure across thirty client sites in a single afternoon

cons.claim: Single-stack commitment concentrates platform risk and can outgrow its fit
cons.example: a client needing real e-commerce forces either an awkward shoehorn or an out-of-stack exception build

failure_modes: choosing the stack per project by novelty and ending up maintaining five ecosystems
adopting a stack whose export is proprietary, quietly trapping clients against the ownership promise
acceptance_tests: the stack decision record scores the chosen stack against maintainability at portfolio scale, exit portability, hosting fit, security surface, and edit speed, and names the exception process
revisit_triggers: the platform changes its license, pricing, or export capability
performance-budget failures recur across sites on the current stack

nodes.definition: Maintain a constrained library of pre-built, brand-skinnable sections - hero, services grid, testimonial band, gallery, contact block, hours-and-map footer - plus a fixed type scale and a small set of layout patterns, so a new small-business site is assembled and skinned rather than designed from a blank canvas. Per client, only tokens change: logo, palette, photography, copy. Structure, spacing, and interaction behavior stay proven. The library is versioned so old sites can be patched confidently, and it is the mechanism that makes a fixed-price build profitable while keeping quality uniform across the portfolio.

included: fixed type scale and layout patterns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: review feedback or defect data shows a library section systematically underperforming

pros.claim: Assembling from proven sections cuts a build from weeks to days with mobile behavior already tested
pros.example: a plumber and a florist get structurally identical services grids that read as different brands purely through token skinning

cons.claim: Clients who compare notes can perceive sameness, and a truly distinct brand may not fit the section vocabulary
cons.example: a high-end interior designer whose portfolio demands editorial layouts the library does not offer

failure_modes: forking a one-off component per client and re-owning every future update for it
letting the library drift unversioned so no one knows which sites carry which section behavior
acceptance_tests: new sites are composed only of versioned library sections plus tokens, and any bespoke section is logged as a priced exception with an owner
revisit_triggers: a section repeatedly draws review complaints or fails quality checks
a new niche in the client base needs a section type the library lacks

nodes.definition: Turn the build order into a concrete page plan sized for a local small business: a home page that answers who, what, and where in one screen; one page per core service; a proof page (reviews, portfolio, credentials the business actually holds); and a contact page whose call-to-action matches how the business really takes work - call, form, or booking link. Every page gets one stated job and one primary action. On rebuilds the plan is drawn against the crawl of the old site so each existing URL has a designated successor. On-page hygiene (titles, heading order, local-business contact markup) is included as craft and never sold as a ranking promise.

included: page inventory with one job and one primary action each
conversion path matched to how the business takes work
successor mapping for legacy URLs on rebuilds

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the client's services, locations, or intake channel change enough to alter the page inventory

pros.claim: A one-job-per-page plan keeps a small site persuasive and cheap to maintain
pros.example: a five-page heating-and-cooling site where every service page ends in the same tap-to-call action stays coherent instead of sprawling

cons.claim: Compressing a business into few pages can bury a service the owner cares about
cons.example: a salon owner insisting each of twelve treatments needs its own page, tripling the content burden the package priced for

failure_modes: planning pages before content responsibilities are agreed, so the plan promises pages nobody will feed
drawing a rebuild plan without crawling the old site first
acceptance_tests: every planned page has a stated job and primary action, and on rebuilds every legacy URL maps to a successor page or a deliberate retirement
revisit_triggers: the client's service mix changes mid-build
the old-site crawl reveals high-value legacy pages the plan lacked

nodes.definition: Run content collection as a pipeline with teeth, not an open request: a structured questionnaire per planned page (what the business does, differentiators, proof), a media checklist (logo files, usable photos, licenses), one named client contact, and a content deadline tied to the schedule. The teeth are the proceed-with-drafts rule agreed at kickoff: if content misses the deadline, the operator drafts professional copy from the questionnaire and the business's public materials and the build proceeds, with the client correcting at staging review. Client content is the number-one schedule killer in this business, and the pipeline exists so one stalled client cannot clog the build queue.

excluded: copy quality and media preparation standards

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: queue metrics show content wait time dominating delivery time despite the deadline rule

pros.claim: Deadline plus drafts keeps the build queue moving through client silence
pros.example: a restaurant that went quiet for three weeks still launches on schedule because menu copy was drafted from their printed menu and corrected in one review round

cons.claim: Operator-drafted copy can misstate specifics only the owner knows
cons.example: a drafted line about same-day service that the shop does not actually offer must be caught at staging review

failure_modes: open-ended waiting that turns a fixed-fee build into an unpaid parking lot
accepting photos with no stated source or license into the media pack
acceptance_tests: each planned page has an intake pack or a recorded invocation of the proceed-with-drafts rule, and every image carries a stated source and license
revisit_triggers: late content recurs across a niche, suggesting the questionnaire is too heavy
drafted copy repeatedly needs heavy correction at review

nodes.definition: Set the writing and media bar every page must clear before build: copy in the business's own voice that states services, service area, and proof plainly; no fabricated claims on the client's behalf - no invented review counts, credentials, or guarantees the business does not hold; images resized and compressed to the display sizes the design system expects; descriptive alt text written at preparation time, not retrofitted; and only media the client owns or has licensed. Copy corrections happen at the document stage, because rewriting inside built pages is where fixed-fee margin dies.

included: copy honesty rule against fabricated claims

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a licensing or false-claim incident traces back to the preparation standards

pros.claim: Preparing media to spec before build removes the single largest cause of slow pages
pros.example: a six-megabyte phone photo becomes a correctly sized compressed image before it ever touches staging

cons.claim: Strict standards add a preparation pass to every asset even under deadline pressure
cons.example: hand-writing alt text for forty gallery photos of fencing installations the night before the staging reveal

failure_modes: pasting a supplied brochure verbatim, including claims the business cannot support
pulling images from the open web with no license and exposing the client to a demand letter
acceptance_tests: every page's copy is client-approved or flagged under the drafts rule, and every image passes the size budget, carries alt text, and has a recorded source
revisit_triggers: a claim in shipped copy is contested by the client or the public
the design system changes its expected image dimensions

nodes.definition: Execute every build in the same fixed order on a private staging environment: instantiate the stack and design system, apply brand tokens, assemble pages per the plan, pour prepared copy and media, wire navigation, footer, and tap-to-call, connect forms, run the responsive pass at phone widths first, then sweep for internal defects before the client sees anything. The same order every site makes omissions visible as unchecked boxes and lets a substitute builder read exactly where a half-done job stands. Nothing is ever built or rebuilt on the live domain.

included: internal defect sweep before client reveal

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in stack or design system alters the build stages themselves

pros.claim: A fixed sequence makes progress measurable and the work delegable
pros.example: a subcontractor picks up a half-finished build and reads from the checklist exactly which stages are complete

cons.claim: Checklist discipline feels heavy on a three-page site and tempts skipping under pressure
cons.example: skipping the internal sweep on a 'simple' site sends the client a staging link with a broken mobile menu as their first impression

failure_modes: editing the live site during business hours instead of staging
pouring unapproved raw content and building every page twice
acceptance_tests: the staging URL is private and search-engine-excluded, and every checklist stage is recorded per site before the client reveal
revisit_triggers: the offer adds features or section types the stage list does not cover
defect data shows one stage repeatedly failing across sites

nodes.definition: Treat the contact form as the revenue-carrying feature it is. Forms must submit reliably; spam protection must not punish legitimate customers; notifications must be sent from an authenticated address on a domain with aligned SPF and DKIM so they reach the owner's real inbox; and every submission must also be stored server-side where it can be retrieved when email fails. The test is end-to-end: a real submission travels to the owner's actual inbox and the owner confirms receipt. A visually perfect site that silently drops leads is the worst deliverable this business can ship, because the client discovers it weeks later as missing customers.

included: end-to-end inbox test with owner confirmation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a deliverability change at major mail providers alters what authenticated sending requires

pros.claim: Authenticated notifications plus stored submissions make lead loss detectable and recoverable
pros.example: when a notification bounces, the week's enquiries still sit in the site's submission log for retrieval

cons.claim: Aggressive spam protection blocks the real customers it was meant to protect
cons.example: a strict puzzle challenge turning away the older customers of a mobility-equipment shop

failure_modes: sending form mail 'from' the visitor's own address and failing DMARC at the client's mail provider
testing only to the operator's inbox and never to the client's actual mailbox
acceptance_tests: a live test submission reaches the client's own inbox and is confirmed by the client
submissions are stored server-side and retrievable
the sending domain passes SPF and DKIM alignment checks
revisit_triggers: the client reports enquiries that never arrived
a mail provider tightens its authentication policy

nodes.definition: Run client review as bounded, structured rounds instead of an open comment stream: the client sees a complete staging site, never a half-built one; feedback is collected into one consolidated list per round mapped to pages; the build order's revision allowance is restated at round start; in-scope corrections are executed together; and out-of-scope requests are logged to a written change-order or care-plan backlog rather than argued live. The round ends in written sign-off, and sign-off is the trigger for launch preparation - the workflow's whole job is convergence.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: review-round counts or duration trend up across the client book

pros.claim: Consolidated rounds converge feedback that would otherwise dribble in for weeks
pros.example: nine scattered emails become one round-two list executed together in an afternoon

cons.claim: Batching frustrates clients who want each tweak visible immediately
cons.example: an anxious first-time owner reads 'I am saving your notes for the round' as being ignored

failure_modes: revealing an incomplete build and burning the first impression the review depends on
treating every request as in-scope to avoid an awkward conversation
acceptance_tests: each round has a dated consolidated list with every item marked in-scope or routed out, and final written sign-off exists before launch preparation begins
revisit_triggers: rounds repeatedly exceed the revision allowance
one section or page type attracts recurring feedback across clients

nodes.definition: Hold every site to the same pre-launch bar regardless of price: all links resolve; forms are tested end-to-end; phone numbers are tap-to-call; name, address, and hours are consistent across the site and match the client's public listings; a spelling pass is done; the legal basics are present (privacy notice and whatever cookie disclosure the client's jurisdiction requires - verify current rules where the client operates); favicon and social-share metadata are set; a 404 page exists; and the staging search-exclusion flag is scheduled for removal at launch, not before and not forgotten. The gate is binary: an unmet item blocks launch or is explicitly waived in writing with a reason.

included: consistency with the client's public listings
visitor-side test results for every third-party integration

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: warranty-window defect categories reveal a missing check

pros.claim: A binary gate catches the small breakages that erode client trust in week one
pros.example: the QA pass catches the old phone number surviving in the footer copy carried over from the crawl

cons.claim: Gate rigor on trivial items can delay a launch the client urgently needs
cons.example: holding a go-live for a missing favicon while the client's ad campaign start date slips past

failure_modes: shipping with the staging search-exclusion flag still on, making the new site invisible
an inconsistent business name or number across pages contradicting the client's public listings
acceptance_tests: the checklist run is recorded per site with each item marked pass or waived-with-reason, and no unwaived failure exists at launch
revisit_triggers: post-launch defects recur in a category the checklist lacks
a jurisdiction changes its disclosure obligations

nodes.definition: Enforce a per-site performance budget expressed as mechanisms and proven by measurement, and speak about speed only in terms the measurement supports. The mechanisms: images compressed to display size, system fonts or a strictly limited webfont set, no plugin or script without a job, and host-level caching enabled. The proof: a repeatable lab measurement on a throttled mobile profile, recorded before and at launch. Any performance claim made to the client must be reproducible from the recorded run - 'your site scores this on this test, here is the run' - never a superlative that cannot be re-run by a skeptic.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the lab tool's scoring model or the dominant device profile of local visitors changes

pros.claim: Recorded measurements make speed a demonstrable deliverable instead of a vibe
pros.example: the launch report includes before-and-after runs for a rebuilt site so the improvement is checkable by anyone

cons.claim: Lab scores vary run to run and chasing the last few points has steep diminishing returns
cons.example: burning hours to nudge a score while the client's uncompressed photo shoot remains the honest bottleneck

failure_modes: quoting a speed claim a fresh run cannot reproduce
adding a heavy feature during review that quietly busts the budget with no re-measurement
acceptance_tests: a dated measurement run at launch is stored in the runbook and any client-facing speed statement cites it
revisit_triggers: the measurement tool changes its scoring model
budget failures cluster on one section type or plugin

nodes.definition: Bake an accessibility floor into the design system so every shipped site clears it without per-site heroics: readable contrast in every brand-token combination, keyboard-navigable menus and forms, labeled form fields, alt text on meaningful images, focus states left intact, heading hierarchy preserved, and text alternatives when video or audio is used. Accessibility legal exposure is an obligation class that varies by jurisdiction and keeps shifting, so the operator describes the floor honestly - a WCAG-informed baseline, not a certified audit - and flags 'verify current rules where the client operates' for clients in regulated sectors instead of selling compliance the operator cannot warrant.

excluded: legal advice on any jurisdiction's statute

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: accessibility regulation or enforcement practice changes in a served jurisdiction

pros.claim: A floor built into the templates costs near zero per site once established
pros.example: contrast-safe token pairs mean no per-client color fight after a brand palette arrives

cons.claim: A baseline is not a certified audit, and saying so costs some sales sheen
cons.example: a client serving government customers needs a real third-party audit the operator must source externally

failure_modes: promising absolute legal compliance as a product feature
skinning brand tokens that silently break contrast on buttons and links
acceptance_tests: each launch records the baseline checks passed, and every client-facing description calls it a baseline rather than a certification
revisit_triggers: the obligation class shifts in a jurisdiction where clients operate
an accessibility complaint or demand letter arrives for any portfolio site

nodes.definition: Establish, before any technical change, that the domain sits in an account the client owns and controls: registrar account in the client's name with the client's payment method and recovery email, the operator working through delegated collaborator access instead of holding the login, and auto-renew confirmed against a working card. If the domain currently lives in a previous developer's or a defunct agency's account, recovering it into client control is a project task in its own right and precedes any cutover. The operator never transfers a client domain into the operator's own account: client ownership is the exit guarantee, and this business keeps clients through service quality, never by holding the domain.

included: client-named registrar account with client payment method
recovery of stranded domains before cutover
excluded: registering client domains under the operator's own account

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a registrar policy change or a domain-loss incident anywhere in the portfolio

pros.claim: A client-owned registrar makes departures clean, which itself sells trust
pros.example: a departing client leaves in a day with no leverage games and tells two other shop owners exactly that

cons.claim: Client-held accounts add coordination friction at exactly the moments speed matters
cons.example: waiting two days mid-migration for an owner to approve a registrar confirmation email

failure_modes: registering client domains under the operator's account 'for convenience' and creating a de facto hostage
an expired card on the client's registrar account letting the domain lapse silently
acceptance_tests: the registrar account shows the client as owner with their payment method and recovery email
operator access is delegated and revocable rather than a shared login
auto-renew is confirmed on and recorded in the runbook
revisit_triggers: the registrar changes its delegation or transfer features
the client-side person who owns the account leaves the business

nodes.definition: Treat the client's existing email as untouchable infrastructure during any web work. Before anything changes, inventory where mail is hosted and which DNS records carry it - MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and any webmail or autodiscover subdomains - and replicate them verbatim into the new zone if nameservers move. Web hosting changes never implicitly move or break mail; if the client also wants email changes, that is a separately planned migration with its own window. A small business can survive a day without its website as an inconvenience; a day without email is invoices, orders, and customer replies silently bouncing - the single fastest way this business loses a client and earns a horror-story reputation in a small town.

included: mail-hosting and mail-record inventory before any change
separation of email migrations from web cutovers

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any mail-flow incident during a cutover anywhere in the portfolio

pros.claim: Verbatim mail-record replication makes web cutovers boring for email
pros.example: a nameserver move the owner never notices because MX, SPF, and DKIM landed identical in the new zone

cons.claim: Treating mail as frozen defers fixing genuinely broken mail configuration found during inventory
cons.example: discovering a missing SPF record but scheduling the fix as a separate change window instead of bundling it into the cutover

failure_modes: switching nameservers to the new host's defaults and dropping the MX records outright
copying MX but forgetting SPF and DKIM so mail still arrives while the client's outbound quietly lands in spam
acceptance_tests: a pre-change zone export exists and identifies every mail-carrying record
the post-change zone contains identical mail-carrying records
a send-and-receive test on the client's own mailbox passes after cutover
revisit_triggers: the client changes email provider
DMARC reports or bounce complaints appear after any DNS change

nodes.definition: Plan every DNS change as a staged, reversible operation: full zone export first; prefer the minimal change - repointing the web records only - over a wholesale nameserver move whenever the current DNS host is serviceable; lower TTLs a day ahead so both the switch and any rollback propagate fast; schedule the switch in a low-traffic window that is not a Friday evening; keep the old hosting live through propagation; and hold a written rollback that one person can execute alone. The plan states exactly which records change, which must not change (the mail records per the safeguard), who executes, and how success is verified: site resolving on the new host, certificate valid, redirects live, mail test passing.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a propagation or rollback incident shows the staging assumptions were wrong

pros.claim: Minimal-change cutovers shrink the blast radius to the website alone
pros.example: repointing a single A record migrates the site while the client's mail, booking subdomain, and forgotten FTP relics stay untouched

cons.claim: Staged cutovers take calendar days that a 'just switch it tonight' client resents
cons.example: explaining why TTL lowering today means the real switch happens Thursday, not in the next ten minutes

failure_modes: a nameserver move without re-creating the full zone at the new DNS host
cutting over with no rollback while the old hosting account is already cancelled
acceptance_tests: the written plan lists the exact records changing, the records preserved, the TTL schedule, the rollback steps, and the post-switch verification results with timestamps
revisit_triggers: the hosting target or DNS host changes
a cutover incident review finds a step the plan template lacks

nodes.definition: Make HTTPS and baseline hardening a standard launch deliverable, not an upsell: certificate issued and its auto-renewal verified rather than assumed; HTTP-to-HTTPS and www/apex canonical redirects in place; no mixed-content warnings; admin accounts unique per person with strong authentication - the client's owner-level access documented and held by the client, the operator working day-to-day on a separate least-privilege account; stack and extension versions current at launch; and login endpoints protected against trivial brute force. Ongoing patch cadence belongs to care-plan operations; this node ends at a hardened, documented state on launch day.

included: per-person credentials with client-held owner access
excluded: ongoing patching and monitoring after handoff

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: certificate tooling, authentication norms, or an incident change the launch hardening bar

pros.claim: Verifying auto-renewal at launch kills the classic month-three 'your site says not secure' call
pros.example: forcing a renewal test during launch week proves the host's automation actually fires

cons.claim: Hardening adds friction for the client's own legitimate access
cons.example: an owner annoyed at being asked to use a password manager for their editor login

failure_modes: a certificate issued once whose renewal silently fails ninety days later
one shared admin login reused across multiple client sites
acceptance_tests: HTTPS resolves with a valid certificate and forced redirect, the renewal mechanism has been observed to fire, and the credential inventory shows client-held owner access plus operator least-privilege access
revisit_triggers: the host changes its certificate tooling
a credential leak or breach notice touches any account in the portfolio

nodes.definition: On any rebuild of an existing site, preserve the web equity the business already earned. Crawl the old site while it is still up and archive its URL list and content; map every legacy URL to a successor page as a 301, or to a deliberate retirement with the closest relevant target; keep the page titles the business is known by unless there is a reason to change them; and after cutover verify that old URLs actually redirect and that external touchpoints - the business profile link, social bios, directory listings, printed QR codes - land somewhere sensible. No ranking outcome is promised; the honest commitment is narrower and testable: no inbound link or listing the business already earned will hit a 404 because of this rebuild.

included: pre-launch crawl and archive of the old site
post-cutover verification of redirects and external touchpoints

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: post-launch 404 or listing-breakage reports on any rebuilt site

pros.claim: The redirect map converts rebuild risk into a checkable list
pros.example: a chiropractor's decade-old article URL cited on a local forum still lands on the relevant new page after launch

cons.claim: Exhaustive mapping of a large legacy site costs hours the fixed fee did not envision
cons.example: an eight-hundred-URL legacy site of expired event pages needing triage into map-versus-retire

failure_modes: launching before crawling, so the old URL set is unrecoverable once the old host is gone
blanket-redirecting every legacy URL to the home page and calling it continuity
acceptance_tests: the crawl archive exists before launch, the map covers every crawled URL, and post-launch spot checks confirm the redirects respond
revisit_triggers: webmaster tooling shows 404s accumulating after launch
the client reports a printed QR code or directory link failing

nodes.definition: Execute launch as a scripted run, not an event: confirm every upstream gate passed (QA, performance, accessibility, written sign-off); execute the DNS cutover plan; remove the staging search exclusion; verify HTTPS end to end; run the redirect spot checks; submit the sitemap in webmaster tooling owned by the client; re-run the form-to-inbox test on the live domain because staging cannot exhibit live mail routing; wire analytics under the client's own account; and then hold a defined post-launch watch window - the first one to three days - actively checking propagation, mail flow, and form submissions rather than waiting for a panicked call. The launch report is written as the run happens, each verification timestamped with its outcome.

included: live-domain re-tests of forms and HTTPS
post-launch watch window with a named owner
excluded: ongoing monitoring beyond the watch window

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a launch-day incident exposes a missing verification in the script

pros.claim: A scripted launch turns the most stressful hours of the project into a checklist
pros.example: the live-domain form test catches a mail-routing difference that staging could never exhibit

cons.claim: Watch-window vigilance is unbilled attention stretched across evenings and weekends
cons.example: a Friday-evening launch quietly obligating weekend propagation checks - the reason the script forbids Friday launches

failure_modes: launching and walking away during propagation
forgetting to remove the staging search exclusion - the classic invisible-site error
acceptance_tests: the launch report records each verification with timestamp and outcome, and the watch window is scheduled with a named owner before the run starts
revisit_triggers: watch-window incidents recur in a category the script lacks
the cutover plan template changes upstream

nodes.definition: Close the build by putting the client in genuine possession of their property and the skills matching their appetite: a handover pack listing every asset and account - domain registrar, hosting, site admin, analytics, form logs - with who holds which credential; owner-level access confirmed in the client's hands; a short training session, ideally recorded, covering the edits the client says they want to make themselves (text, photos, hours); and a plain statement of what the completed build includes versus what the care plan covers, so day-two expectations are set. Handover honesty is the real sales pitch for the care plan: the client stays because service is easier than self-managing, never because leaving is impossible.

included: recorded training scoped to the client's appetite

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: ticket volume shows trained clients repeatedly asking for the same taught edits

pros.claim: A recorded walkthrough dramatically cuts repeat how-do-I questions
pros.example: the bakery re-watches the two-minute clip on changing holiday hours instead of opening a ticket

cons.claim: Training invites well-meaning owner edits that break layouts
cons.example: an owner pasting a word-processor document into a page and shattering the type scale

failure_modes: a handover pack promised but never assembled once the final invoice is paid
training pitched at a technical level the owner cannot absorb, leaving them owning nothing in practice
acceptance_tests: the handover pack is delivered and acknowledged, and the client either demonstrates one real edit during training or explicitly declines self-editing
revisit_triggers: staff turnover on the client side removes the trained person
the care plan changes what is self-serve versus done-for-you

nodes.definition: Write the per-site runbook during the build, because it is the operational memory hosting and care operations will run on: stack and extension versions with licenses; where the site is hosted and how to reach it; the DNS zone as launched; credential locations referencing the password manager entries, never plaintext secrets in documents; form and mail routing; the launch performance measurement; decisions and exceptions such as bespoke sections or waived QA items; and the warranty-window terms. The test of a good runbook: a competent stranger could take over the site's care tomorrow without emailing the builder - which is exactly what the client-ownership promise requires if the client ever leaves.

included: versions, hosting, as-launched DNS, routing, measurements, decisions, warranty terms
credential references to the password manager

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an incident where the runbook failed to answer a takeover question

pros.claim: Takeover-ready documentation turns the portfolio from personal knowledge into a delegable, even sellable, asset
pros.example: a vacation-week emergency handled end to end by a contractor working purely from the runbook

cons.claim: Documentation discipline is unpaid time per site and rots the moment updates skip it
cons.example: a runbook still naming the old form plugin that a later fix replaced, misleading the person debugging lost leads

failure_modes: reconstructing DNS from memory during an incident because no as-launched zone was stored
credentials scattered across email threads instead of referenced from the password manager
acceptance_tests: the runbook exists at handoff with every section filled, and a second person - or a self-review against the takeover checklist - confirms it is actionable without the builder
revisit_triggers: any post-launch change to the site
the care team reports a gap or a stale entry

nodes.definition: Gate the transition from project to recurring relationship with a definition-of-done: launch report complete with no unwaived failures; client sign-off on the live site; domain confirmed client-owned with delegated access; handover pack delivered; runbook complete; an initial backup taken and its restore point confirmed on the hosting side; warranty-window terms - what post-launch fixes are included and for how long - stated in writing; and the site formally enrolled into whichever care tier was sold, the tier's contents being whatever the offer defined, never renegotiated here. A site that skips this gate becomes the unowned orphan that generates late-night emergencies and cancels quietly a year later.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the care operation reports intake gaps traceable to the gate checklist

pros.claim: An explicit gate prevents launched-but-orphaned sites
pros.example: the gate catches that backups were never enabled on a site launched in a rush, before it enrolls in care billing

cons.claim: Gate ceremony delays recurring revenue recognition for stragglers
cons.example: a client who will not schedule their training session keeps the project file open for a month

failure_modes: silently rolling a site into care billing without its runbook or backup baseline
leaving warranty terms verbal so every post-launch request becomes a negotiation
acceptance_tests: every gate item is recorded as passed, any failure blocks enrollment with the failed item named, and the warranty terms exist in writing
revisit_triggers: care-plan intake requirements change
warranty claims on recent launches exceed the expected pattern

nodes.definition: Small-business sites rarely stand alone: the booking widget, the ordering menu, the review carousel, the map, the chat bubble and the payment link are other companies' code running inside the client's page. Treat each as an integration with an owner, a test and a fallback rather than a snippet pasted where it fit. Per embed the operator records which account it belongs to - the client's own vendor account, never the operator's - what it costs the page in weight and third-party requests, what it stores in the visitor's browser so the privacy notice can be honest about it, and how a human proves it works from the visitor's side: a real test booking, a test order the owner confirms landing in their dashboard. Every embed also gets a stated degraded behavior, because a vendor outage must never take the phone number, address and opening hours down with it.

included: per-embed record of the owning client vendor account
measured weight, request and browser-storage cost of each embed
visitor-side functional test per integration, confirmed by the owner
documented degraded behavior when a vendor is slow or unavailable
excluded: choosing or contracting the client's booking, ordering or payment vendor

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a vendor changes or retires an embed used across several portfolio sites, or a launched integration is found to have been silently failing between the widget and the owner's dashboard

pros.claim: An embed inventory with owner-confirmed tests turns other companies' code into a checkable deliverable
pros.example: a test reservation made from a phone during staging review shows the restaurant owner the booking arriving in their vendor dashboard before launch instead of after a lost Saturday

cons.claim: Every integration widens a surface the operator can neither patch nor version
cons.example: a review-widget vendor changes its script months later and the testimonials band renders empty across a dozen portfolio sites in the same week

failure_modes: pasting an embed that runs under the operator's own vendor account, so the client's bookings quietly depend on the operator's login
accepting 'it renders' as the test and never making one real transaction the owner confirms receiving
letting a chat or analytics embed set browser storage the site's privacy notice never mentions
acceptance_tests: every embed on the site is listed with its owning client account, a dated visitor-side test result the owner confirmed, its measured cost against the page budget, and its documented behavior when the vendor is unavailable
revisit_triggers: a vendor changes its embed code, its pricing, or what it collects
an integration is added or swapped during review rounds

nodes.definition: The client on the other end of this project usually cannot verify a single technical claim the operator makes, which is exactly why the delivery-side communication standard is written down and held rather than left to mood. Progress is described in plain language and in terms of what the owner will be able to do, not in stack and plugin vocabulary. Every claim travels with the evidence behind it - the recorded measurement, the redirect check, the form test - and no claim is made that a skeptic could not re-run. Risk is disclosed before agreement is asked for, so a cutover window and its worst case are an informed choice rather than a surprise. The client's fear of downtime, hacking or lost rankings is never used as leverage to sell an extra, a faster launch or a bigger care tier. Where the owner is elderly, unwell, working in a second language or plainly out of their depth, the operator slows down, puts it in writing, and offers to include an employee or family member the owner trusts instead of accepting a rushed yes.

included: plain-language progress and risk explanation to a non-technical owner
every claim paired with a test that can be re-run on request
written informed consent before irreversible steps
no fear-based selling during delivery; added care where the owner cannot evaluate the work
excluded: sales conversations, package pricing and care-tier recommendation, which belong to the offer stage
the technical content of the cutover plan itself

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a dispute, refund request or lost referral traces to an expectation the delivery communication failed to set in writing

pros.claim: Disclosure-first delivery produces the referrals this business actually runs on, because the client can repeat what was done and why
pros.example: an owner who was told plainly that email is the risky part of a cutover, and then watched the mail test pass, tells the next shop owner exactly that story

cons.claim: Full disclosure can frighten a nervous owner into delaying a launch that is genuinely ready
cons.example: a dentist postpones the cutover twice after the rollback plan is explained in detail, pushing an otherwise finished build weeks past its window

failure_modes: reporting progress in stack and plugin terms the owner cannot evaluate, so their 'yes' carries no information
raising a security or ranking scare to close an extra in the middle of delivery
taking a verbal go-ahead for an irreversible step from an owner who visibly did not understand it
acceptance_tests: before any irreversible step the client holds, in writing, what changes, what could break, how recovery works and how long it takes, plus their explicit go-ahead
every performance, continuity or security statement in a client-facing document names the test that produced it and can be re-run on request
revisit_triggers: the client signals confusion, anxiety, or that someone else decides for them
a complaint or dispute traces back to something the client says they were never told

edges.why_related: the section library is built in and versioned against the one chosen stack
the page plan concretizes exactly the pages and features the build order enumerates
the per-page questionnaire and media checklist are generated from the page plan
collected content is what the copy and media bar is applied to before build
the build pours only prepared, licensed, size-budgeted content into pages
the build assembles versioned library sections rather than designing from scratch
form wiring and deliverability testing happen on the assembled staging build
review rounds start only once the checklist says the staging site is complete
the QA gate runs on the signed-off build so corrections do not invalidate checks
the end-to-end form test is one of the binary items the gate verifies
the accessibility floor is implemented once inside the library's sections and tokens
the mail-record inventory requires access to the client-controlled DNS and registrar
no cutover is planned until the domain is confirmed in the client's control
the cutover plan's preserved-records list comes from the mail inventory
certificate issuance and redirect verification follow the DNS pointing the plan executes
each legacy URL's successor target is defined by the new page plan
launch begins only with a recorded QA pass or written waivers
the launch run executes the cutover plan as its central step
training and handover happen on the verified live site, not on staging
a complete runbook is one of the gate's pass conditions
no launch step may proceed past a failed mail-flow verification
the gate cannot pass unless the domain is confirmed client-owned with delegated access
a section must fit the performance budget before it joins the library
media preparation must satisfy the alt-text and contrast floor the baseline sets
review-round wish lists pull against the fixed contents of the signed build order
edges.resolution_rule: the build order wins: out-of-scope requests route to a written change order or the care-plan backlog, and only a client-approved change order alters the order

edges.why_related: clients sometimes demand bespoke design outside the section vocabulary mid-review
edges.resolution_rule: within the productized price the library's vocabulary wins; a bespoke section requires a priced written exception logged with an owner and a maintenance note

edges.why_related: rich media the client loves pulls against the measured page-weight budget
edges.resolution_rule: the measured budget wins: media is compressed, cropped, or replaced until the measurement passes, and any deliberate exception is re-measured and documented in the runbook

edges.why_related: waiting for perfect client content pulls against launching on the scheduled window
edges.resolution_rule: after the recorded content deadline the proceed-with-drafts rule fires and the launch window holds; content perfection never blocks launch, and later wording changes ride the care plan

edges.why_related: structured, on-time intake measurably reduces the number and size of review rounds
a clean QA pass at launch drives down warranty-window fix volume at the handoff gate
written sign-off is the event that starts launch preparation
the as-launched DNS zone and the launch measurement are appended to the runbook right after go-live
warranty-window defect categories flow back as new checks on the QA baseline
repeated budget failures on the current stack trigger the stack re-evaluation clause
both are the same discipline at different layers - making sure mail the business depends on actually arrives, one for enquiry notifications leaving the site, one for the whole mail flow of the domain
embeds are wired into the assembled staging pages and tested there, never first on the live domain
each integration's owner-confirmed visitor-side test result is one of the binary items the pre-launch gate reads
vendor widgets the client wants drag third-party scripts that push the page past its measured weight budget
edges.resolution_rule: the recorded measurement decides: an embed that busts the budget is first downgraded to a lighter path - a link-out to the vendor's own page or a static block - and is kept inline only when the client states in writing that the integration is business-critical, with the budget miss recorded alongside it

edges.why_related: the build order fixes what was actually promised, which is the reference every honest progress statement is measured against
no irreversible launch step runs without the client's informed written go-ahead against a plainly stated worst case

conflict_axes.name: repeatable_system_vs_bespoke_design
conflict_axes.description: The section library makes fixed-price builds profitable, while clients periodically want a look the vocabulary does not offer.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the library wins at the productized price; bespoke work exists only as a priced written exception with a named maintenance owner

conflict_axes.name: content_wait_vs_launch_momentum
conflict_axes.description: Waiting for the client's real words and photos produces authenticity, while open-ended waiting stalls the queue and the recurring revenue behind it.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the deadline plus proceed-with-drafts rule agreed at kickoff decides it automatically; drafts are corrected at review, not before build

conflict_axes.name: rich_media_vs_performance_budget
conflict_axes.description: Large hero video and full-resolution galleries please the owner's eye while measurably sinking the mobile experience the budget protects.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the recorded measurement is the referee: compress, crop, or replace until it passes, and document any deliberate exception

conflict_axes.name: review_wishes_vs_signed_scope
conflict_axes.description: Every staging reveal generates ideas that were not sold, and each absorbed freebie retrains the client to expect more.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: route out-of-scope items to a written change order or the care-plan backlog in the same breath as accepting in-scope fixes; goodwill is spent deliberately, not leaked

conflict_axes.name: stack_familiarity_vs_client_portability
conflict_axes.description: The stack easiest for the operator to run at scale is not automatically the one a departing client can take elsewhere, and the ownership promise depends on the exit path.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: portability is a hard criterion in stack selection, not a tiebreaker: a stack with no real export path is disqualified regardless of operator comfort

conflict_axes.name: security_hardening_vs_client_control
conflict_axes.description: Locking accounts down protects the portfolio, while the client's ownership of their own property requires them to hold the highest access.
poles: keep the client in ultimate control
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the client holds documented owner-level access; the operator works on a separate least-privilege account; hardening never becomes a mechanism of lock-in

conflict_axes.name: cutover_speed_vs_dns_safety
conflict_axes.description: Clients and cash flow want the switch tonight, while safe cutovers need TTL lead time, a quiet window, and a live rollback path.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: compress the calendar only by preparation (early TTL lowering, pre-staged records), never by skipping the zone export, the mail check, or the rollback

conflict_axes.name: verifiable_claims_vs_marketing_pressure
conflict_axes.description: Clients ask for ranking promises and speed superlatives, while the honest deliverable is only what a reproducible check can show.
poles: promise outcomes to close and please
claim only what a recorded run demonstrates
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: offer the measurement itself as the deliverable - before/after runs, redirect checks, form tests - and decline outcome guarantees explicitly

conflict_axes.name: gate_rigor_vs_delivery_throughput
conflict_axes.description: Every binary gate protects quality and the care plan's economics, while each gate also holds up launches and the recurring billing that starts after them.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: gates stay binary but waivable in writing with a reason; the waiver log, not gate-skipping, is the pressure valve

conflict_axes.name: client_reassurance_vs_full_risk_disclosure
conflict_axes.description: A nervous owner wants to hear that everything is under control, while honest delivery requires saying plainly what could break at cutover, what a widget collects, and what the operator cannot promise. Reassurance that outruns the evidence is how delivery-stage trust is destroyed the first time something goes wrong.
poles: keep the client calm with a simplified story
disclose the real risk, the evidence and the limits
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclose first, then reassure with mechanism rather than adjectives: name the risk, show the control that contains it - zone export, lowered TTLs, a one-person rollback, the recorded test - and put the worst case and the client's go-ahead in writing before the irreversible step runs

edge_cases.description: The client's domain sits in an unreachable previous developer's personal registrar account
edge_cases.trigger: the access inventory finds the registrar login belongs to someone who no longer answers
edge_cases.mitigation: run registrar recovery with the client's ownership evidence before any build work is scheduled for cutover; never launch on a domain the client does not control, and as a last resort launch on a new client-owned domain with a continuity plan

edge_cases.description: A nameserver switch silently drops the client's email because the mail records were never replicated
edge_cases.trigger: the new DNS host's default zone lacks the MX, SPF, and DKIM entries the old zone carried
edge_cases.mitigation: zone export before any change, verbatim replication of mail-carrying records, and a send-and-receive mailbox test as a blocking post-switch verification

edge_cases.description: The client never sends content and the project stalls unpaid for months
edge_cases.trigger: the content deadline passes with the intake pack still empty
edge_cases.mitigation: invoke the proceed-with-drafts rule agreed at kickoff: draft from the questionnaire and public materials, build on schedule, and correct wording in the review round

edge_cases.description: Form notifications land in spam and the client loses weeks of leads without knowing
edge_cases.trigger: notification mail is sent unauthenticated or 'from' the visitor's own address
edge_cases.mitigation: authenticated sending on an aligned domain, server-side submission storage as the safety net, a live-domain test to the client's real inbox at launch, and a submission check inside the watch window

edge_cases.description: A rebuild launches without redirects and the business's old URLs, listings, and printed QR codes break
edge_cases.trigger: the old site goes offline before it was crawled or the 301 map was skipped
edge_cases.mitigation: crawl and archive while the old site is still up, map every URL before cutover, and spot-check redirects and external touchpoints as launch verifications

edge_cases.description: The client demands a bespoke layout outside the section library in round two of review
edge_cases.trigger: a staging reveal inspires design ambitions the package never included
edge_cases.mitigation: acknowledge the idea, restate the revision allowance, and route the bespoke request to a priced change order with a maintenance note rather than arguing taste live

edge_cases.description: A hero video the owner insists on pushes the page far over the weight budget
edge_cases.trigger: supplied media cannot pass the recorded performance measurement
edge_cases.mitigation: offer the compressed or poster-image alternative, show the before/after runs, and document any client-insisted exception with its re-measured cost

edge_cases.description: The client asks the operator to guarantee a first-page ranking as a launch condition
edge_cases.trigger: sign-off is withheld pending an outcome promise nobody can honestly make
edge_cases.mitigation: decline the guarantee explicitly, present the verifiable deliverables (measurement runs, redirect checks, form tests) as what is warranted, and if needed escalate to the scope's honest-positioning terms

edge_cases.description: The old hosting account is inaccessible on cutover day and nothing can be exported from it
edge_cases.trigger: the previous host or developer refuses or fails to hand over access
edge_cases.mitigation: plan cutovers that need nothing from the old host: public-crawl the content early, rebuild from the archive, and repoint DNS at the registrar the client controls

edge_cases.description: The certificate fails to renew weeks after launch and the site shows security warnings
edge_cases.trigger: auto-renewal was assumed at issuance but never observed to fire
edge_cases.mitigation: verify the renewal mechanism during launch week, record expiry and renewal method in the runbook, and hand the monitoring duty to care operations at the gate

edge_cases.description: An accessibility demand letter arrives for a portfolio site months after launch
edge_cases.trigger: a complainant or firm targets the client's site in a jurisdiction with active enforcement
edge_cases.mitigation: produce the recorded baseline checks, remediate the specific gaps promptly, advise the client to verify current obligations with counsel in their jurisdiction, and fold the gap class back into the template floor

edge_cases.description: A booking or ordering widget keeps rendering after the vendor changes its embed, but silently stops delivering bookings to the owner
edge_cases.trigger: the vendor updates its script or the account behind it lapses, and nobody re-tests the integration from the visitor's side
edge_cases.mitigation: record every embed with its owning client account and a visitor-side test the owner can repeat, re-run those tests at launch and whenever a vendor announces a change, and keep phone number, address and hours in the page itself so a dead widget never removes the way to reach the business

workflow.action: Translate the signed package into a build order
workflow.description: Fix pages, features, content owners with due dates, revision allowance, and schedule anchors
workflow.gate: every page and feature is itemized, each content item has an owner and date, and the client's written acknowledgment exists

workflow.action: Confirm the stack and design-system fit for this job
workflow.description: Verify the default stack serves this client or record a written exception
workflow.gate: the job runs on the default stack, or an exception is written with owner and reason

workflow.action: Inventory domain, DNS, and email before touching anything
workflow.description: Confirm client registrar ownership, take the full zone export, and identify every mail-carrying record
workflow.gate: client-owned registrar confirmed with delegated access, and the zone export identifies MX, SPF, DKIM, and subdomains

workflow.action: Run structured content intake against the deadline
workflow.description: Collect questionnaire answers, media, and licenses per planned page, or invoke the drafts rule
workflow.gate: every page has content received or a recorded drafts-rule invocation by the deadline

workflow.action: Plan the page architecture and the legacy redirect map
workflow.description: Give every page one job and one action; on rebuilds crawl the old site and map every URL
workflow.gate: each page has a stated job and primary action, and every crawled legacy URL has a successor or deliberate retirement

workflow.action: Build the site on staging from the design system
workflow.description: Assemble sections, apply tokens, pour prepared content, wire forms and navigation, run the phone-first pass
workflow.gate: all checklist stages recorded, staging private and search-excluded, internal defect sweep clean

workflow.action: Prove the lead path end to end
workflow.description: Authenticate notification sending, store submissions server-side, test to the client's real inbox
workflow.gate: a live submission reached the client's own inbox with their written confirmation, submissions are also stored server-side, and every third-party booking, ordering or enquiry integration passed a visitor-side test the owner confirmed

workflow.action: Run bounded review rounds to written sign-off
workflow.description: Reveal the complete site, consolidate feedback per round, route out-of-scope items, converge to sign-off
workflow.gate: written sign-off exists and every out-of-scope request is logged to a change order or backlog

workflow.action: Clear the quality, performance, and accessibility gates
workflow.description: Run the binary QA checklist, record the lab performance measurement, verify the accessibility floor
workflow.gate: no unwaived QA failure, a dated measurement run stored, and the accessibility baseline checks recorded

workflow.description: Lower TTLs ahead, change only the planned records, keep mail records identical, hold the rollback ready
workflow.gate: site resolves on the new host, mail send-and-receive test passes, and rollback remained available throughout

workflow.action: Launch, verify live, and hold the watch window
workflow.description: Remove search exclusion, verify HTTPS and redirects, re-test forms on the live domain, watch propagation
workflow.gate: every launch verification recorded with outcome and the watch window scheduled with a named owner

workflow.action: Hand over assets, train the owner, and gate into care
workflow.description: Deliver the handover pack and training, complete the runbook, take the initial backup, write warranty terms, enroll in the sold tier
workflow.artifact: handover pack, runbook, and gate record
workflow.gate: every definition-of-done item passes - ownership confirmed, backup restore point verified, warranty terms written - before care billing starts

priority_rationale: The frame nodes - build order, stack, and the communication standard the client is owed - come first because every downstream hour is spent executing them; intake and design-system work precede the build pass so nothing is assembled twice; integrations, review, quality, performance and accessibility gates precede launch because fixing on staging is cheap and fixing live is public; the domain, email and DNS transition nodes sit before launch because they carry the only failure modes that can damage the client's existing business; and training, documentation and the handoff gate come last because they convert a launched site into a client-owned, care-ready recurring relationship.

dominance_rules.rule: Email continuity dominates every schedule and launch pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: a broken website inconveniences; broken email silently costs the client orders, invoices, and trust - the one failure that ends the relationship and the referral loop
dominance_rules.trigger: any DNS or hosting change that could touch mail-carrying records
dominance_rules.action: block the change until the mail inventory is replicated and the post-change mailbox test passes

dominance_rules.rule: Client ownership of domain and assets dominates operator convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: the business promise is lock-in through service quality, never through holding assets; one hostage incident poisons the local reputation the business runs on
dominance_rules.trigger: any temptation to register, transfer, or hold a client asset under the operator's own account
dominance_rules.action: refuse; establish client-owned accounts with delegated operator access instead, even when slower

dominance_rules.rule: The signed build order dominates review-round wish lists
dominance_rules.rationale: fixed-price economics collapse if reveals silently expand scope, and clients respect a line that was drawn in writing before feelings were involved
dominance_rules.trigger: a review request exceeds the order's pages, features, or revision allowance
dominance_rules.action: log it to a written change order or the care-plan backlog and deliver the in-scope round as planned

dominance_rules.rationale: performance and continuity claims that cannot be re-run by a skeptic are debts waiting to be called in
dominance_rules.trigger: a claim about speed, rankings, or outcomes is requested or drafted
dominance_rules.action: state only what a recorded reproducible check shows, and decline outcome guarantees explicitly

dominance_rules.rule: The performance budget dominates decorative media
dominance_rules.rationale: the mobile visitor on a slow connection is the customer the small business actually gets
dominance_rules.trigger: supplied media fails the recorded measurement
dominance_rules.action: compress, crop, or replace until the run passes; document any client-insisted exception with its measured cost

dominance_rules.rule: The proceed-with-drafts rule dominates indefinite content waiting
dominance_rules.rationale: one silent client must not park a fixed fee and clog the queue that funds the business
dominance_rules.trigger: the content deadline passes without the intake pack
dominance_rules.action: draft from the questionnaire and public materials, build on schedule, correct at review

dominance_rules.rule: An unpassed gate dominates the launch date
dominance_rules.rationale: shipping a known failure converts a schedule slip into a trust breach discovered by the client
dominance_rules.trigger: a QA, performance, accessibility, or cutover verification fails as launch approaches
dominance_rules.action: slip the date or record a written waiver naming the item and reason; never skip silently

dominance_rules.rule: Legacy continuity dominates the clean-slate urge on rebuilds
dominance_rules.rationale: the URLs, listings, and printed codes a business earned are its property as much as the domain
dominance_rules.trigger: a rebuild plan proposes discarding old URLs without a map
dominance_rules.action: crawl first, map every URL to a successor or deliberate retirement, verify redirects after cutover

dominance_rules.rule: Client-held owner access dominates security lockdown preferences
dominance_rules.rationale: hardening that leaves the client unable to control their own property becomes lock-in wearing a security costume
dominance_rules.trigger: an access design would leave the operator as the only owner-level credential holder
dominance_rules.action: put owner-level access in the client's hands, documented; the operator works least-privilege

dominance_rules.rule: A visitor-side test result dominates an integration that merely looks fine
dominance_rules.rationale: third-party widgets fail by rendering perfectly while delivering nothing, and the client discovers it as missing bookings weeks later
dominance_rules.trigger: any embed - booking, ordering, chat, review or payment link - is present on a site approaching launch
dominance_rules.action: make one real test transaction the owner confirms receiving, record it against the embed's owning account, and treat an untestable embed as a blocking gate item or replace it with a link-out to the vendor's own page

dominance_rules.rule: Informed client consent dominates the launch calendar on irreversible steps
dominance_rules.rationale: a cutover, an account move or a decommissioned old host cannot be undone by apology, and a client who did not understand what they agreed to has not agreed
dominance_rules.trigger: a step would change DNS, move an account, or take the previous site offline
dominance_rules.action: state in writing what changes, what could break, how recovery works and how long it takes, obtain an explicit go-ahead, and where the owner is plainly out of their depth slow down and offer to include someone they trust before proceeding

anti_rework_rules.rule: Export the full DNS zone and identify mail records before changing any nameserver or record
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructing lost MX and SPF entries from memory during a live email outage

anti_rework_rules.rule: Lock the page plan and content responsibilities before assembling any page
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding pages twice when late content arrives shaped differently than the layout assumed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Prepare copy and media to standard before the build pass, never inside built pages
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-editing text and re-cropping images across every page after assembly

anti_rework_rules.rule: Crawl and archive the old site before anything is switched off
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unrecoverable redirect map and lost content when the old host account vanishes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Test forms end to end to the client's actual inbox before launch, not after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the emergency rebuild of the lead path after weeks of silently lost enquiries

anti_rework_rules.rule: Get written staging sign-off before starting any launch preparation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: redesign churn on the live site under the client's customers' eyes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run performance and accessibility checks on staging, not first on production
anti_rework_rules.prevents: public-facing fixes and re-measurement after the client has already shared the link

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the runbook during the build, not from memory after handoff
anti_rework_rules.prevents: undocumented sites entering care operations and being reverse-engineered during incidents

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify certificate auto-renewal during launch week rather than assuming it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the month-three security-warning callout and the trust damage that rides with it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm every third-party embed runs in the client's own vendor account and passes a visitor-side test on staging, before the launch window opens
anti_rework_rules.prevents: hunting a booking vendor's login on launch day and rebuilding an integration under the client's live traffic

anti_rework_rules.rule: Put the cutover's worst case, rollback and client go-ahead in writing before the window is booked
anti_rework_rules.prevents: renegotiating an interrupted launch with a frightened owner in the middle of propagation

iteration_protocol.trigger: a warranty-window defect is reported on a recent launch
iteration_protocol.action: fix it, classify it, and add its class to the QA baseline so the next site cannot ship it

iteration_protocol.trigger: a cutover incident touches email or causes downtime
iteration_protocol.action: run a post-incident review and amend the cutover plan template and mail-inventory checklist

iteration_protocol.trigger: the performance budget is missed repeatedly on the current stack or a section type
iteration_protocol.action: diagnose whether the stack, a section, or media practice is at fault and revise or trigger stack re-evaluation

iteration_protocol.trigger: review rounds exceed the allowance across multiple clients
iteration_protocol.action: improve the intake questionnaire and the completeness of the staging reveal so feedback converges earlier

iteration_protocol.trigger: the care team reports missing or stale runbook data during an incident
iteration_protocol.action: extend the runbook template and re-verify the takeover test on recent sites

iteration_protocol.trigger: the platform announces a breaking change, license shift, or export-path degradation
iteration_protocol.action: re-score the stack against the selection criteria and plan a portfolio migration path if it fails

iteration_protocol.trigger: accessibility obligations shift in a jurisdiction where clients operate
iteration_protocol.action: update the baseline floor, re-audit the section library, and schedule remediation for affected sites

iteration_protocol.trigger: a third-party vendor changes or retires an embed used across several portfolio sites
iteration_protocol.action: inventory which sites carry it, re-run the visitor-side test on each, downgrade to a link-out where it cannot pass, and update the integration standard and the affected runbook entries
